doors.note: Own stores: 3 US (NY Madison, Beverly Hills, Dallas Highland Park Village) + London Mayfair + Seoul (Hyundai Apgujeong). Retailers section lists ~25 North America third-party stockists (Bergdorf, Elyse Walker, Kirna Zabete etc.) — not counted.

fibre.sample: stratified sample of 81 of 293 women's RTW styles, proportional by garment group (house product types, with 171 untyped products typed from the title); census f

tech_evidence.names: Aloe Linen (aloe-treated linen); a silver-thread lining against phone radiation (unnamed, 2017)
tech_evidence.share: aloe linen on ~4 of 81 sampled styles

craft_evidence.owned: partial — wool from 'her family's six-generation merino sheep farm in Uruguay' for some suiting (2018); garments made by third parties, mostly in Italy (/pages/sustainability)
craft_evidence.makers: yes — Manos del Uruguay, a women's non-profit cooperative, hand-knits the brand's hand-knits (since 2015; named on PDPs, e.g. the Lawrence sweater); a 'family-run atelier' in Italy for recycled-fur co
craft_evidence.mills: none by name; deadstock, GRS-recycled cashmere, Sea Island cotton from Barbados, 'woven in China, finished in Italy' on some pages
craft_evidence.madein: 73 of 81 sampled pages state a country (Italy 69, Uruguay 2, China 2)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated — first womenswear collection Fall/Winter 2015; Manos del Uruguay partnership since 2015 (/pages/sustainability)
craft_evidence.process: yes — year-by-year sustainability timeline: deadstock shares per collection (60% SS21, 97% of wovens SS26), hand-knitting by the cooperative, own-farm merino suiting, EON digital traceability (2020),
craft_evidence.reasoning: Country of make on 90% of product pages, a named maker for the hand-knits (Manos del Uruguay, since 2015), wool from the founder's family farm and a dated, specific process record. The garment factories themselves are unnamed and not owned, which keeps it from a 5. 4.
